explain.say: Have you noticed how many prices end in 99? Shoes for 999 rupees, a toy for 4 dollars 99. Why not just 1,000 or 5? Look at the coin on the board. To your brain, 4.99 often feels like four-something, not almost five!

explain.say: See the eye? We read numbers from left to right, and our brain grabs the first digit fastest. In 4.99 the first digit is 4; in 5.00 it's 5. Scientists call this the left-digit effect. Which first digit does your brain notice in 299?

faq.a: Our brains pay most attention to the first digit of a price. So 2.99 feels much closer to 2 than to 3, even though it's just 1 cent less than 3.

faq.q: Did 99 prices start to stop cashiers stealing?
faq.a: That's a popular story: an odd price meant the cashier had to open the till for change, which recorded the sale. Historians aren't sure it's the real reason.

faq.q: Do 99 prices really make people buy more?
faq.a: Many studies and shop tests suggest they often do, especially for everyday items, because the price feels lower.

faq.q: Why do some fancy shops use round prices?
faq.a: Round prices like 50 or 200 can feel classy and simple, so some luxury shops avoid 99 endings on purpose.

faq.q: How can I avoid being tricked by 99 prices?
faq.a: Round the price up in your head: 4.99 is 5, and 999 is 1,000. Then compare prices fairly.

facts: Prices ending in 9 or 99 are known as charm prices or psychological prices.
The left-digit effect means people judge a price mostly by its first digit.
